input_api: new DatagramDnsResponseDecoder() / new DatagramDnsQueryDecoder() in an EmbeddedChannel, fed new DatagramPacket(ByteBuf, recipient, sender)
scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: Netty DNS codec (DnsResponseDecoder, DnsMessageUtil, DefaultDnsRecordDecoder, DnsCodecUtil)
family_note: Own Java decoder; Vert.x's DNS client and Netty's DnsNameResolver use it. Netty leaves A/AAAA (and MX/CNAME after decompression) as raw records, so the harness formats addresses from the decoded bytes and reads names with the public DefaultDnsRecordDecoder.decodeName. DnsQuery carries no AA/TC/RA/RCODE; they are reported as 0 for the query control.

name: pcap4j-core
license_evidence: Parent POM org.pcap4j:pcap4j:1.8.2 (sha256 a53d00da...) declares <name>MIT License</name>, checked in the image; the jars carry no license file
input_api: org.pcap4j.packet.DnsPacket.newPacket(byte[] rawData, int offset, int length) throws IllegalRawDataException
documentation_note: The javadoc documents the static newPacket(byte[], int, int) factory, which builds a DnsPacket from raw DNS message bytes. The README documents pcap4j-packetfactory-static as the runtime packet-factory module; without it Pcap4J cannot build DNS RDATA.
scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: Pcap4J DNS packet classes (DnsPacket, DnsDomainName, DnsResourceRecord, DnsRData*)
family_note: Own Java decoder inside the Pcap4J packet library (pinned to 1.8.2, the latest non-pre-release; 2.0.0-alpha.6 is the deps.dev default). The documented DnsPacket.newPacket(byte[], int, int) decodes a DNS message from caller-supplied bytes; no capture handle, interface or libpcap call is used (JNA is on the class path but never loads a native library). RDATA comes from the documented runtime module pcap4j-packetfactory-static 1.8.2. Pcap4J keeps the reserved Z bit, AD and CD. Names are decompressed with the documented DnsDomainName.decompress(message); for a name that is only a compression pointer Pcap4J returns a leading '.', which the harness drops. AAAA text is formatted by the harness from the decoded 16 bytes (RFC 5952). Its deps.dev count covers the whole multi-protocol pcap4j-core artifact. Coverage and AFL++ features are scoped to Pcap4J's DNS classes (org.pcap4j.packet.Dns*, namednumber.Dns*, StaticDnsRDataFactory and util.ByteArrays): building the first RDATA loads the static factory binder, which initialises every protocol's named-number tables (TcpPort, UdpPort, IpNumber and others) and would otherwise make up most of the response control's features.

family_note: Own Java decoder of the MiniDNS project (formerly de.measite.minidns, an old coordinate of the same code that is not counted); the minidns-core artifact holds the message model and parser, while the resolver and client live in other artifacts that the harness does not load. MiniDNS decodes AD and CD but not the reserved Z bit, so z carries AD and CD only (both controls have all three bits clear). Names are DnsName.ace (lower-cased ACE text); A text is MiniDNS's own toString; AAAA text is formatted by the harness from the decoded 16 bytes (RFC 5952), because MiniDNS prints uncompressed groups.

license_evidence: POM nl.sidnlabs:dnslib:0.2.20 (sha256 b035fa49...) declares 'GNU General Public License, version 3', checked in the image; the upstream SIDN/dns-lib repository's LICENSE is GPL-3.0 and the source headers carry the GPL-3.0 notice. scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: SIDN dnslib (ENTRADA: Message, Header, Question, RRset, ResourceRecordFactory per-type decoders, DNSStringUtil, NetworkData)
family_note: Own Java decoder of SIDN Labs (the .nl registry), written for its ENTRADA DNS analytics platform and published separately as nl.sidnlabs:dnslib; it uses no other DNS library (Guava's InetAddresses only formats the decoded IPv6 address, commons-codec only encodes DNSSEC and TXT fields). The harness constructs NetworkData over the caller's bytes and calls the Message constructor; no ENTRADA, pcap or network code is loaded. dnslib keeps the reserved Z bit, AD and CD. Each section is held as RRsets keyed by owner, class and type in first-seen order; the harness lists the records of each RRset in order (the controls have one record per RRset) and reports the section counts from those lists. OPT records are moved out of the additional section into the message's pseudo field (the controls have none). Types and classes are the raw values the library read; names are the library's lower-case text, to which the harness adds the trailing dot. A text is InetAddress.getHostAddress() and AAAA text is the library's own Guava InetAddresses.toAddrString (RFC 5952). Low adoption: deps.dev counts 13 direct dependents over its releases. Found through a Maven Central artifact-id prefix search (a:dns*).

The header codec reads the three bits after RA as a lenient constant, so none of Z, AD and CD is kept and z is reported as 0 (both controls have all three bits clear). Question and record classes are decoded as a 1-bit mDNS flag (unicast-response/cache-flush, false for both controls) plus a 15-bit class. A/AAAA are java.net.Inet4Address/Inet6Address built from the decoded bytes: A text is getHostAddress(), AAAA text is formatted by the harness from getAddress() (RFC 5952).
